hints: With $F = 0$, only the 75 N force along the positive x-axis and the 50 N force at $60^\circ$ above the positive x-axis act.
Find resultant magnitude $R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + 43.30^2} \approx 109\text{ N}$ and direction $\theta = \arctan(Y/X) \approx 23.4^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive x-axis.
walkthrough:
Resolve the forces along the x-axis and y-axis with $F = 0$, $G = 75\text{ N}$, and $\alpha = 60^\circ$:
$$X = 75 + 50\cos 60^\circ = 75 + 50(0.5) = 75 + 25 = 100\text{ N}$$
$$Y = 50\sin 60^\circ = 50\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3013\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R$:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + (25\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{10000 + 1875} = \sqrt{11875} \approx 108.97\text{ N} \approx 109\text{ N}$$

Calculate the direction angle of the resultant:
$$\theta = \arctan\left(\frac{Y}{X}\right) = \arctan\left(\frac{43.3013}{100}\right) = \arctan(0.433013) \approx 23.413^\circ \approx 23.4^\circ$$
$$\text{Direction: } 23.4^\circ \text{ anticlockwise from the positive x-axis}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Resolve all active forces into rectangular components along the Cartesian axes:
- Force $G = 75\text{ N}$ acts directly along the positive x-axis: $(75, 0)$.
- Force $50\text{ N}$ acts at angle $60^\circ$ above the positive x-axis: $(50\cos 60^\circ, 50\sin 60^\circ)$.

Sum the components along the x-axis:
$$X = 75 + 50\cos 60^\circ = 75 + 25 = 100\text{ N}$$

Sum the components along the y-axis:
$$Y = 50\sin 60^\circ = 50 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3013\text{ N}$$

Apply the Pythagorean formula to determine the resultant magnitude:
$$R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + (43.3013)^2} = \sqrt{10000 + 1875} = \sqrt{11875} \approx 108.972\text{ N} = 109\text{ N} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

Determine the direction angle relative to the positive x-axis:
$$\theta = \arctan\left(\frac{Y}{X}\right) = \arctan\left(\frac{43.3013}{100}\right) \approx 23.413^\circ = 23.4^\circ \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
State the direction clearly: $23.4^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive x-axis.

hints: With $G = 0$, resolve forces horizontally: $50\cos\alpha - F\cos 50^\circ = 0 \implies 50\cos\alpha = F\cos 50^\circ$.
Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to eliminate both $50$ and $F$: $\tan\alpha = \frac{3 + \sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ}$.
Solve for $\alpha = \arctan(5.8589) \approx 80.3^\circ$, then substitute $\alpha$ back to find $F = \frac{50\cos 80.3^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} \approx 13.1\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium ($G = 0$):
$$50\cos\alpha - F\cos 50^\circ = 0 \implies 50\cos\alpha = F\cos 50^\circ \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$50\sin\alpha - 3F - F\sin 50^\circ = 0 \implies 50\sin\alpha = F(3 + \sin 50^\circ) \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 2 by Equation 1 to eliminate $50$ and $F$:
$$\frac{50\sin\alpha}{50\cos\alpha} = \frac{F(3 + \sin 50^\circ)}{F\cos 50^\circ} \implies \tan\alpha = \frac{3 + \sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ}$$
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{3 + 0.766044}{0.642788} = \frac{3.766044}{0.642788} \approx 5.85892$$

Substitute $\alpha = 80.312^\circ$ into Equation 1 to solve for $F$:
$$F = \frac{50\cos 80.312^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ} \approx \frac{50(0.168267)}{0.642788} = \frac{8.41337}{0.642788} \approx 13.0888 \approx 13.1$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation for coplanar forces at point $P$:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies 50\cos\alpha - F\cos 50^\circ = 0$$
$$50\cos\alpha = F\cos 50^\circ \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies 50\sin\alpha - 3F - F\sin 50^\circ = 0$$
$$50\sin\alpha = F(3 + \sin 50^\circ) \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 2 by Equation 1 to eliminate both $50$ and $F$ simultaneously:
$$\frac{50\sin\alpha}{50\cos\alpha} = \frac{F(3 + \sin 50^\circ)}{F\cos 50^\circ}$$
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{3 + \sin 50^\circ}{\cos 50^\circ}$$

Compute the numerator and denominator using trigonometric values:
$$\sin 50^\circ \approx 0.766044 \implies 3 + \sin 50^\circ \approx 3.766044$$
$$\cos 50^\circ \approx 0.642788$$
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{3.766044}{0.642788} \approx 5.85892$$

Take the inverse tangent to find the angle $\alpha$:
$$\alpha = \arctan(5.85892) \approx 80.312^\circ = 80.3^\circ \text{ (to 1 d.p.)}$$

Substitute $\alpha = 80.312^\circ$ back into Equation 1 to find $F$:
$$F = \frac{50\cos(80.312^\circ)}{\cos 50^\circ} \approx \frac{50 \times 0.168267}{0.642788} \approx \frac{8.41336}{0.642788} \approx 13.0888 = 13.1 \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
